name: climate.countries
summary: Each country's mean temperature from its own record (CRU TS 4.07, 1901 to 2022, via the World Bank portal) regressed on the global anomaly (HadCRUT5, re-zeroed to 1850 to 1900): the slope is the country's observed share of global warming, the intercept its level. The run's global anomaly from the energy module times the slope gives the country's annual mean each year; the hottest month moves by the same slope from its 1991 to 2020 mean. Pattern scaling from the record; the stated assumption is that the pattern persists.

name: people.wetbulb
summary: Days per year of dangerous afternoon wet-bulb temperature at each country's capital, and the people in those countries. Ten observed years of daily maximum temperature and mean dew point at the weather station nearest the capital (NOAA GSOD) give a daily afternoon wet-bulb (Stull 2011); each is shifted by the country's warming at constant relative humidity and the days over two published limits counted. Exposure at one city per country, not a death toll; a crossing event the first year a capital passes a limit on more than days_to_cross days.

views.title: what this run does not yet measure
views.source: Not in this run, so not in these numbers: deaths from heat (a published exposure-response layer is next), harvests and food prices, forest cover and the carbon it would release, biodiversity, fresh water, sea level from ice, migration, and any response by people to any of it. The population here is the UN's path, which assumes none of the above changes where people live. Every crossing above is a count of people living where a stated limit is passed, not a toll, and the model runs about 0.15 °C warm in 2024.
